incoming.name: Sumatra
incoming.excerpt: Ibn Battuta, who visited the kingdom during his journey, pronounced the kingdom "Sumatra", hence the name of the island.

outgoing.name: Afghanistan
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: From there he journeyed south to Afghanistan, the mountain passes of which he used to cross into India.

outgoing.name: Aral Sea
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: After a month in the city, he retraced his route to Astrakhan, then carried on past the Caspian and Aral Seas to Bokhara and Samarkand.

outgoing.name: Baghdad
outgoing.section: To Iran and the Silk Roads
outgoing.excerpt: Next were Shiraz and Baghdad, the latter of which was in bad shape after being sacked by Hulagu Khan.

outgoing.name: Beijing
outgoing.excerpt: He also travelled even further north, through the Grand Canal to Beijing, although there has been some doubt about whether this actually occurred.

outgoing.name: Black Sea
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: From there he travelled by land to Konya and then Sinope on the Black Sea coast.

outgoing.name: Caspian Sea
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: After a month in the city, he retraced his route to Astrakhan, then carried on past the Caspian and Aral Seas to Bokhara and Samarkand.

outgoing.name: China
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: Eventually he resolved to leave on the pretext of taking another hajj, but the Sultan offered the alternative of being ambassador to China.

outgoing.name: Delhi
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: Spending another year there, he then resolved to seek employment with the Muslim Sultan of Delhi.

outgoing.name: Eritrea
outgoing.excerpt: Spending about a week in each of his destinations, he visited Eritrea, Ethiopia, Mogadishu, Mombassa, Zanzibar, and Kilwa, among others.

outgoing.name: Iran
outgoing.excerpt: His next destination was the Il-Khanate in modern-day Iraq and Iran.

outgoing.name: Maldives
outgoing.excerpt: He resolved to carry on to China, with a detour near the beginning of the journey to the Maldives.

outgoing.name: Mecca
outgoing.excerpt: At the age of (approximately) twenty Ibn Battuta went on a hajj — a pilgrimage to Mecca.

outgoing.name: Muhammad
outgoing.excerpt: After spending Ramadan in Damascus, Ibn Battuta joined up with a caravan travelling the 800 miles from Damascus to Medina, burial place of Muhammad.

outgoing.name: Oman
outgoing.excerpt: Having completed his final adventure before settling down, he then immediately decided to go visit Oman and the Straits of Hormuz.

outgoing.name: Shanghai
outgoing.excerpt: From there he went north to Hangzhou, not far from modern-day Shanghai.

outgoing.name: Timbuktu
outgoing.excerpt: Dubious about the miserly hospitality of the king, he nevertheless stayed for eight months before journeying back up the Niger to Timbuktu.

outgoing.name: Timur
outgoing.section: To Iran and the Silk Roads
outgoing.excerpt: From there he journeyed to Basra, then Isfahan, which was only a few decades away from being nearly destroyed by Central Asian warlord Timur.

outgoing.name: Turkey
outgoing.section: Byzantine Empire, Anatolia, Central Asia and India
outgoing.excerpt: A sea voyage from Damascus on a Genoese ship landed him in Alanya on the southern coast of modern-day Turkey.

outgoing.name: Vietnam
outgoing.excerpt: This time he succeeded, reaching in quick succession Chittagong, Sumatra, Vietnam, and then finally Quanzhou in Fujian Province, China.
